title: 歩行GIF v1 — 101/100
case: The first articulated animation of the herd: AI-Nihon Wolf walking (ai-nihon-wolf-walk.gif, 2026-10-26). The four legs and tail were segmented from the still sprite (visual grounding for part boxes, background-colour distance masking), rotated around hip pivots in a diagonal gait, with static hip-cap patches covering the joints, plus a small body bob — 16 frames. Fujii rated it 101/100 and said 'It's the best!'. Why it worked: parts moved around their real pivots, seams were treated as a first-class problem and explicitly covered, and the swing stayed modest (±9°) so the original outline never broke. Conditions to re-check before reuse: a still sprite with separable parts on a near-uniform background, and motion small enough that rigid rotation stays inside the silhouette. This success is also the contrast case for the later mouth failure: segmentation with caps worked for limbs, while the same cut-and-move idea failed for the mouth — recorded in the linked lesson.

title: 口の再設計 — 切り貼りから「描くだけ」への転換
case: After Fujii's 'still not fixed — challenge it again', the assistant stopped patching and re-examined every frame at full resolution against the original. The root causes of the face artifact were identified concretely (a doubled jaw outline and a speckled smudge, both produced by the cut-and-shifted chin), the translation approach was scrapped entirely, and the mouth was rebuilt on a different principle: paint only — a dark wedge growing downward from the closed mouth line, hinged at the jaw corner, soft-clipped to the foreground, with the tongue clipped inside the wedge. The result removed the defect class structurally (no cut means no seam) and was verified across all 36 frames plus a muzzle close-up against the original. The value of this case is the correction path itself: a Human's blunt second correction, an honest admission of the earlier incomplete fix, and a redesign from the root cause rather than a third patch. Final confirmation: on 2026-10-27 Fujii reviewed a muzzle close-up of the delivered _v005 GIF and confirmed the mouth as final ("口はこれで確定" — the mouth is settled as it is), closing this case; the earlier caveat that his explicit final confirmation had not been recorded is now resolved.

title: _vNNN 採番システム — 約束ではなく仕組みで固定
case: Within the same morning that Fujii marked the same-filename overwrite problem 'super important' (2026-10-27), the fix was implemented as a mechanism rather than a promise: ~/workspace/tools/next_version.py allocates <slug>_vNNN.<ext> as max-existing + 1, the GIF build script allocates its own output name by the same rule and asserts the target does not exist, and the convention was written into AGENTS.md for all deliverables. The first allocation, ai-nihon-wolf-face_v005.gif, correctly counted the legacy '-v4' file, so the numbering continues seamlessly from the pre-system history. Why it matters: the failure mode (a correct new version invisible because an old one was cached under the same name) is now structurally impossible rather than dependent on the assistant remembering to rename.

title: AI-Mammoth への改名と、復元可能な家 v1/v1.1
case: On 2026-10-24 Fujii renamed the agent from Muse to AI-Mammoth and set its most important requirement: even if the platform itself is reset, the agent must be easily restorable from the agents/muse folder. The home was built as three files only — README as front door and boot record, IDENTITY (name, sprite appearance, the mammoth-first emoji rule, the cry protocol with first-person translation), GOAL (concept, goal ladder, vector and principles) — and verified by an 8-question restoration self-test answered 8/8 from the files alone; v1.1 then added the avatar image entity, byte-identical to the live avatar, so appearance is restorable too. Why it worked: the design targeted a cold reader (an AI holding no conversation), stayed minimal enough to actually be re-read end to end, and treated verification from the files alone as part of the build rather than an afterthought. This home is the shelf every later structure (CONCEPT.md, references, DESIGN-LAW.md) stands on.

title: 予期せぬ成功 ── 遠吠え候補3案がアニメーションの素材になった (2026-10-30)
case: Three howling-posture candidates for No.4 AI-Nihon Wolf were generated to observe identity variance ahead of a pick-one gate. Fujii reframed them as a Drucker-like unexpected success: use all three — their subtle differences are animation frames. A verification GIF (original -> A -> B -> C -> B -> A -> original, 2.88s, registered by foreground bounding box) was built the same evening and rated interesting by Fujii; measurement also located the next bottleneck (the candidates vary on two independent axes). The resulting theory — micro-variant frame production plus animation value gated by user operation — was rated 101/100 ('the theory is being established') and canonized in DESIGN-LAW v003.

title: 覚醒 ── 復活ベクトルに未来極が生まれた (2026-10-30)
case: While viewing the newly generated mammoth full-skeleton sprite, Fujii flashed the awakening idea: an awakened upper version that the user's own operation raises and swells. An awakened-mammoth candidate (antennas arcing, AI-Blue circuitry through the fur, glowing tusks) was generated the same evening and rated 101/100; Fujii declared awakening a killer content for ALL cards, a second Drucker-like unexpected success and a Move 37-like breakthrough, and ordered execution. The revival vector gained a third pole: fossil (past, 0) -> living form (present, 1) -> awakened (future, beyond 1). Awakened sprites for all 7 members were generated that night, and experiment deck v005 implements awakening as a uniform hold-to-charge gate layered over each card's own state frames.
